title: Normal stalks of full root algebras along a regular divisor
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative regular ring [def-weil-regular-scheme], let $f\in R$ have injective multiplication, and assume $R/(f)$ is regular. Let $m\geq0$ and let $e_k$ for $k\in\operatorname{Fin}m$ be positive integers invertible in $R$. Put $B=\prod_kR[T]/(T^{e_k}-f)$ and $N=\operatorname{Spec}B$ [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. For every point $z\in N$, the stalk $\mathcal O_{N,z}$ is an integrally closed domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]. Empty products and zero rings are allowed.

source.place: Tag 0EYH, localizations over (f) in the proof; Tag 0EYG, full root algebra in the strictly henselian calculation

proof.text: Each monic root algebra B_k=R[T]/(T^{e_k}-f) is finite free over Noetherian R, hence Noetherian. Freeness makes multiplication by f injective on B_k. For the root coordinate t, t^{e_k}=f; therefore multiplication by t is injective too.

At a prime containing t, quotient the local ring by t. This is a localization of R/(f), hence a regular local ring. Lifting regularity across a nonzerodivisor gives regularity of the local ring itself. At a prime not containing t, both f and e_k*t^{e_k-1} are units, so the localized algebra is etale over the regular base and is regular. This is the local verification in Tag 0EYH.

Regular local rings are integrally closed domains. A prime of a finite product belongs to one factor with the same localization. The scheme stalk is that localization, giving both conclusions. For m=0 there are no points, so the assertion is vacuous. For unit f all primes fall in the etale case.

lean.statement: theorem regular_divisor_root_model_normal (R : CommRingCat.{u}) [IsRegularRing R] (m : ℕ) (f : R) (hf : IsSMulRegular R f) [IsRegularRing (R ⧸ Ideal.span {f})] (e : Fin m → ℕ) (he : ∀ k, 0 < e k ∧ IsUnit (e k : R)) : let N := Spec (CommRingCat.of (∀ k : Fin m, AdjoinRoot ((Polynomial.X : Polynomial R) ^ e k - Polynomial.C f))) ∀ z : N, IsDomain (N.presheaf.stalk z) ∧ IsIntegrallyClosed (N.presheaf.stalk z)
